finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::sql read-only guard is bypassable: comment stripping ignores string literals, letting a crafted query smuggle extra statements into the interpolated wrapper in executequery
evidence: Verified against the supplied sources: sql-validator.ts:29-31 strips `--...` and `/*...*/` with plain regexes before any quote handling, and the only string-literal handling (`replace(/'[^']*'/g,'')`, ~line 53) happens afterwards, so a `--` inside a literal erases the rest of the query from the validator's view. Hand-tracing the reviewer's payload `SELECT '--' ) AS q ; DROP TABLE t ; SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT 1` gives `withoutComments === "SELECT '"`, which passes the first-token, forbidden-keyword, and single-statement checks; datasource.service.ts then interpolates it into `SELECT * FROM (${dto.query}) AS _q LIMIT 10001`, and `client.query(text)` with no values uses pg's simple query protocol, which executes the three `;`-separated statements including the DDL under the datasource's decrypted credentials. Two caveats: the flaw is pre-existing (this diff only adds pg type parsers and `SET TimeZone`/`SET DateStyle`, it does not touch the validator), and exploitation requires a workspace member who already has query access — but the read-only guard is the sole boundary being defeated, hence critical.
